title: Rapid Isolation of Viable Circulating Tumor Cells from Patient Blood Samples
protocol: Sonicate 250 μL of halloysite nanotube solution (6.6 wt% in water) at 10-13 W (rms) for 30 seconds.
Cool the sonicated solution with cold water and repeat sonication once more.
Draw the sonicated and filtered halloysite nanotube solution into a syringe.
Attach a 0.45 μm syringe filter to the syringe and filter the solution into a clean microfuge tube.
Vortex the solution occasionally to maintain homogeneity.
Obtain a 50 cm long section of Micro-Renathane microtubing with an inner diameter of 300 μm and an inner volume of 35.3 μL.
Cut one end of the microtube at a diagonal and attach it to a small IDEX adaptor piece.
Insert the needle of a 3/10 cc 29G syringe into the other end of the microtube.
Clean the microtube by placing its open end (the end with the adaptor) into 70% ethanol.
Draw approximately 50 μL of ethanol into the syringe to fill the microtube completely.
Rinse the ethanol out of the microtube by drawing a generous volume of distilled water into the syringe.
Prepare a solution of 0.02% w/v poly-L lysine in water and draw 50 μL into the microtube.
Allow the poly-L lysine solution to sit for 5 minutes at room temperature (RT).
Draw 100 μL of filtered nanotube solution into the microtube and allow it to incubate for 3 minutes at RT.
Draw 100 μL water through the microtube to rinse out the nanotube solution.
Allow coated microtube to sit, filled with water, overnight at RT.
Prepare a solution of 10 μg/mL protein G in 1X Dulbecco's phosphate buffered saline (PBS, pH 7.0 - 7.2).
Draw 50 μL PBS through the microtube and then draw 50 μL of the protein-G solution.
Allow to incubate for 1.5 hr at RT.
Prepare a solution containing 5 μg/mL E-selectin-IgG and 50 μg/mL antibody (anti-EpCAM for most cancer samples, anti-PSMA for prostate cancer samples) in PBS.
Draw 50 μL of the E-selectin and antibody solution into the microtube.
Allow to incubate for 2 hr at RT.
Prepare a solution of 5% (w/v) milk protein in PBS.
Draw 50 μL milk protein solution into the microtube.
Allow to incubate for 1 hr at RT.
Draw 50 μL PBS into tube and leave at RT until blood or buffy coat samples are ready for processing.
Prepare a solution of PBS saturated with Ca2+ ("PBS+") 10 min prior to using the microtube for isolation.
Draw 50 μL PBS that has been saturated with Ca2+ into the microtube.
Place 10 mL Ficoll-Paque lymphocyte isolation solution into a 50 mL centrifuge tube.
Gently layer 10 mL whole blood on top of Ficoll without mixing.
Centrifuge at 2000x g for 15 min at 4 °C with minimal deceleration.
Remove the buffy coat layer and place in a new tube.
Wash buffy coat with PBS (centrifuge at 230x g for 10 min, discard supernatant).
Gently resuspend cells with 1 mL RBC lysis buffer and incubate for 10 min at room temperature to lyse erythrocytes.
Add 10 mL PBS, mix gently, and centrifuge at 230x g for 10 min.
Discard the supernatant and gently resuspend the pellet in 3 to 4 mL PBS+.
Attach one end of the functionalized microtube to a 5 mL syringe using IDEX adaptors.
Insert the syringe onto a syringe pump.
Submerge the open end of the functionalized microtube into the cell suspension.
Process the cell suspension through the microtube at 1 to 4 mL/h.
Transfer the open end of the microtube to a tube containing PBS+ and draw 300 μL PBS+ into syringe at 0.016 mL/min to remove unbound and loosely bound cells from the microtube.
Place the open end of the microtube into a clean tube.
Disconnect the syringe from the microtube and attach a syringe prefilled with Accutase.
Gently perfuse enough Accutase into the microtube to fill (~50 μL) and allow to incubate at room temperature for 10 min.
Attach a syringe prefilled with 1 mL of growth media (79% RPMI, 20% FBS, 1% penicillin streptomycin).
Perfuse into microtube, collecting effluent into tissue culture treated well plate.
Culture cells at 37 °C and 5% CO2 under humidified conditions.
